title: Iya Valley: vine bridges and hidden hamlets
includes: Private guiding in English or Dutch
Transport in my car from Tokushima or Oboke
Thermos tea and a simple picnic if we skip restaurants
excludes: Lunch (we stop at a local place; budget ¥1,500–2,500)
Your hotel pickup outside Tokushima/Oboke (ask — often possible)
description: The Iya Valley is the Shikoku that still feels folded away: cedar slopes, a river far below, villages that lost their young people and kept their roofs. We cross one of the kazurabashi vine bridges, walk a quiet hamlet, and take the road that rental cars usually miss. This is not a theme-park Japan day. It is weather, woodsmoke, and enough walking to earn lunch. I time the bridges before the tour buses, then spend the afternoon where the valley goes quiet again.

title: A day on the 88 Temple trail
includes: Private guiding in English or Dutch
Nōkyōchō stamp assistance if you bring a book
Context on Kōbō Daishi and how modern henro actually walk
excludes: Temple stamp fees (a few hundred yen each)
meetingPoint: Tokushima Station, or your lodging in the eastern circuit
description: You do not need to walk 1,200 kilometres to understand the Shikoku pilgrimage. One well-chosen day — three or four temples, a stretch of real path, a bowl of something hot — is enough to feel why people still do this. I pick a section that matches your legs: gentler temple clusters near Tokushima, or a hillier pair if you want the staff and the sweat. We go as guests, not as collectors. I’ll show you how to bow, when to stay quiet, and where the vending-machine coffee tastes like a reward.

title: Seto Inland Sea: coast, citrus, slow ferries
includes: Private guiding in English or Dutch
Car and ferry fares for the planned route
Time in a fishing town and a lookout above the water
excludes: Art-island museum tickets if we add Naoshima/Teshima (priced separately)
description: The Inland Sea is Shikoku’s other face: olive groves, rusted shipyards, islands that look close enough to swim to. We follow the water rather than a museum list. Depending on ferries and your taste, we might thread a fishing harbour, a citrus grove, and a stretch of coast where the Seto bridges hang in the haze. If you specifically want the art islands, say so in your inquiry — that becomes a different, ticketed day. Otherwise we stay with salt air, udon, and the unfashionable towns I prefer.

title: Oboke Gorge and the Yoshino River
includes: Private guiding in English or Dutch
excludes: Pleasure-boat ticket if we take it (usually under ¥2,000 pp)
description: Oboke and Koboke cut a green, almost alpine gorge through the heart of the island. In high summer the river is a rafting scene; on a weekday in shoulder season it is mostly water, rock, and a two-car train. We walk the lookouts, take the little boat if the water is calm, and eat somewhere unremarkable and good. Pair this with Iya if you have two days — they sit next to each other on the map and in the mind.

title: A day built around you
includes: Planning by email before you arrive
Private guiding in English or Dutch
excludes: Admissions, ferries, and meals unless we say otherwise
meetingPoint: Agreed when we plan the day
description: Families with a slow walker. Photographers who want dawn in the hills. People who already did Naoshima and now want a farm, a sake brewery, or nothing listed online. Write and tell me the constraints. I’ll propose a route, a meeting point, and an honest price. Custom days fill faster in cherry blossom and autumn colour — look at the calendar first.
